chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Harith ibn Ja'far, from Ali ibn Isma'il ibn Yaqtin, from Isa ibn al-Mustafad Abu Musa al-Darir, who said: Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrated to me, saying:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Was not Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) the scribe of the bequest, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) the one who dictated it, while Jibra'il and the proximate angels (peace be upon them) were the witnesses?'

He said: So he (the Imam) remained silent for a long time, then said: 'O Abu al-Hasan! What you said did occur, but when the command came down upon the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), the bequest descended from the presence of God as a sealed document. Jibra'il descended with it along with the trustworthy ones of God — Blessed and Exalted — from among the angels. So Jibra'il said: O Muhammad! Command those in your presence to depart, except your successor, so that he may take it from us, and you may make us witness to your handing it over to him as his guarantor — meaning Ali (peace be upon him).

So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) commanded those in the house to depart, except Ali (peace be upon him), while Fatimah was between the curtain and the door. Then Jibra'il said: O Muhammad! Your Lord conveys His greetings to you and says: 'This is the document of what I covenanted with you, and stipulated upon you, and witnessed upon you, and made My angels witness upon you — and it suffices with Me, O Muhammad, as Witness.'

He said: The joints of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) trembled, and he said: O Jibra'il! My Lord — He is al-Salam, and from Him is peace, and to Him peace returns. The Mighty and Majestic has spoken truth and fulfilled His promise. Bring the document! So he gave it to him and commanded him to hand it over to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), and he said to him: Read it! So he read it letter by letter. Then he said: O Ali! This is the covenant of my Lord — Blessed and Exalted — to me, His stipulation upon me, and His trust. I have delivered, counselled, and fulfilled it.

Ali (peace be upon him) said: And I bear witness for you — may my father and mother be your ransom — you have conveyed, counselled, and been truthful in all you said. And my hearing, my sight, my flesh, and my blood bear witness to it for you. Then Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said: And I am among the witnesses for both of you in this.

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: O Ali! Have you taken my bequest, recognized it, and guaranteed to God and to me that you will fulfill what is in it? Ali (peace be upon him) said: Yes — may my father and mother be your ransom — the guarantee of it is upon me, and upon God is my aid and success in fulfilling it.

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: O Ali! I wish to make witness upon you that you will present it to me on the Day of Resurrection. Ali (peace be upon him) said: Yes, make witness! The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Surely Jibra'il and Mika'il are present between us now, and with them the proximate angels — so that I make them witness upon you. He said: Yes, let them witness! And I — may my father and mother be your ransom — make them bear witness.

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) made them witness. Among what the Prophet stipulated upon him, by command of Jibra'il (peace be upon him) in accordance with God's command — Mighty and Majestic — was that he said to him: O Ali! Will you fulfill what is in it: of loyalty to those who are loyal to God and His Messenger, and disavowal and enmity toward those who are hostile to God and His Messenger, and disavowal from them — with patience from you, suppression of anger, the loss of my right, the usurpation of your khums, and the violation of your sanctity? He said: Yes, O Messenger of God.

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: By the One Who split the grain and created the soul, I heard Jibra'il (peace be upon him) say to the Prophet: O Muhammad! Inform him that the sanctity — which is the sanctity of God and the sanctity of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) — will be violated, and that his beard will be dyed from his head with fresh blood.

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: So I was struck with awe/fainted when I understood the statement from the Trustworthy Jibra'il, until I fell on my face. And I said: Yes, I accept and am content — even if the sanctity is violated, the traditions suspended, the Book torn apart, the Ka'ba demolished, and my beard is dyed from my head with fresh blood — patient and seeking reward from God, forever, until I come before you.

Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) summoned Fatimah, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, and informed them similarly to how he had informed Amir al-Mu'minin. They said the same as his statement. The bequest was then sealed with seals of gold that had not been touched by fire, and it was handed over to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): May my father and mother be your ransom — will you not tell me what was in the bequest? He said: The laws of God and the laws of His Messenger. I said: Was the bequest about their seizing power and their opposition against Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him)? He said: Yes, by God — matter by matter, letter by letter.

Have you not heard the word of God — Mighty and Majestic: 'Indeed it is We who give life to the dead and write what they sent ahead and their traces; and We have enumerated everything in a clear Register.' (Ya-Sin 36:12)

By God, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to Amir al-Mu'minin and Fatimah (peace be upon them both): Did both of you not understand what I informed you of, and have you both accepted it? They said: Yes, indeed, and we are patient over what pains and angers us.

And in the copy of al-Safwani there is an addition: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Abu Abd Allah al-Bazzaz, from Hariz, who said: I said to Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him)...

May I be your ransom! How short is your remaining time, O People of the Household, and how close your appointed terms one to another — despite the people's need for you! He said: Indeed, for each one of us there is a scroll in which is what is needed to be done in his appointed time. When what is in it of what he was commanded is exhausted, he knows that his appointed term has arrived. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) then came to him announcing his own death, informing him of what awaits him with God. And al-Husayn (peace be upon him) read his scroll which was given to him, and what was to come of the death announcement was explained to him. And there remained in it things yet unfulfilled, so he went out for battle.

And those were the matters that remained: the angels had asked God to aid him, and He permitted them. They stayed preparing and readying for battle, until he was killed. So they descended — and his time had already ended, and he had been killed (peace be upon him). The angels said: O Lord! You permitted us to descend, and You permitted us to aid him. We descended, and You had already taken him.

So God revealed to them: Stay by his grave until you see him come out, then support him. Weep over him and over what you missed of aiding him — for indeed you have been designated for his aid and for weeping over him. So the angels wept in consolation and grief over what they missed of aiding him. When he comes out, they will be his supporters.

key_terms.الرَّجْعَةُ: Raj'ah — the return of the Imams before the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.الصَّحِيفَةُ: Parchment/scroll — the divine record prescribing each Imam's mission and term
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ: The proximate angels — those closest to God, present as witnesses
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةُ: The bequest — the divine covenant and testament delivered to the Prophet and entrusted to Ali (as)
key_terms.دَمٍ عَبِيطٍ: Fresh blood — foretelling Ali's martyrdom by a wound to the head
key_terms.ضَامِناً: Guarantor — Ali (as) takes responsibility for the bequest's fulfillment
key_terms.كِتَاباً مُسَجَّلًا: A sealed/inscribed document — emphasizing its heavenly origin and inviolability

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith about the Prophet's bequest to Imam Ali and the divine covenant witnessed by Jibra'il?
ai.summary: This lengthy narration, transmitted through Imam Musa al-Kadhim (as) from Imam al-Sadiq (as), describes the celestial bequest delivered to the Prophet (saww) just before his death. The bequest descended directly from God, brought by Jibra'il with angels as witnesses, and was handed to Ali (as), who pledged to fulfill it — including bearing patiently the usurpation of his rights, the seizure of khums, and even the martyrdom foretold for him and the Ahl al-Bayt. A supplemental narration from the copy of al-Safwani reveals that each Imam has a divine parchment prescribing their mission, and recounts how al-Husayn (as) went to Karbala to fulfill remaining obligations in his parchment, while angels who had been permitted to aid him arrived too late, and were commanded to guard his grave until his return.
